# Notes (season 2, planning turn @ day 32, before-season check)

## Where we are
- Day 32 of season 2 (Jan/early Feb) — before the Apr–Nov nightly-decision window opens.
  Budget $2000 and PTO 10 are both untouched; no bookings, no rejects. Nothing to react to yet.
- Season 2 trips so far (doy 1–32, n=192) confirm winter is dead for yellowtail: hd_am/hd_pm/
  twilight/three_quarter/overnight all 0.0 ypa; day_1_5 basically 0 too (3 yt / 392 anglers =
  0.008 ypa). No surprises — matches season 1's winter pattern. Nothing actionable here.

## Data caveats (unchanged)
- `sla`, `glider`, `chl` are STILL 0 rows. Persona leans on sea-level-anomaly but it's not
  populated — keep using `upwelling` (cuti/beuti) + `pier` SST as proxies. Recheck each planning
  turn.
- Season 1 is still the only complete season of trip data. Season 2 real signal starts in April.

## New this turn: ONI/PDO/MEI — season 2 opens in a stronger, more sustained La Niña than season 1
- Season 1 ONI path: opened at +1.31 (moderate El Niño) at doy9, declined all year, crossed zero
  around doy190, ended at -1.54 (La Niña) by doy344. So season 1 warmed the coast early
  (spring/summer) and only went cold by the back half.
- Season 2 opens already at ONI -1.57, PDO -2.04, MEI -1.85, NPGO +0.70 at doy9 — i.e. season 2
  starts where season 1 *ended*, and by these other indices (PDO/MEI) looks even more strongly
  La Niña than season 1's fall trough was. Only one season-2 ONI reading so far; watch how it
  evolves (deepens vs relaxes) as more climate rows post through spring/summer.
- Key implication: season 1's best window (fall run, doy ~290–330) happened *while* ONI was
  already solidly negative (-1.0 to -1.4) — so basin-scale La Niña did NOT prevent the fall bite.
  This supports last turn's finding that local trailing signals (pier SST 7d, CUTI 14d) matter
  more than the big ONI number for timing. Don't use ONI as a gate.
- But: season 2 being La Niña-flavored *all year*, not just by fall, is an untested situation —
  season 1 data can't tell us whether a colder spring/summer baseline shifts or shrinks the fall
  window, or dampens it overall. Treat the Oct–Nov window as the working hypothesis, not a
  certainty, and lean on live signals (fishdope narrative, pier SST trend, CUTI trend) starting
  ~August to confirm or revise before committing PTO/budget in September.

## Standing plan (carried over, lightly adjusted)
- Never book HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT for yellowtail — near-zero all season, both years so far.
- Primary target: DAY_1_5 and OVERNIGHT trips in the Oct–Nov fall window (doy ~290–330), same as
  season 1's clear best window. Budget ~2–3 DAY_1_5 ($550 ea) + a few OVERNIGHT ($400) trips
  there; fill with a couple THREE_QUARTER ($150) if budget allows.
- Given the La Niña-all-year risk above, don't front-load PTO/budget purely on the season-1
  calendar pattern. Starting ~doy 230–260 (Aug), watch: trailing 14-day CUTI (falling = good),
  trailing 7-day pier SST (rising = good), and fishdope narrative/yt_all mentions. If these look
  materially weaker than season 1's equivalent period, be ready to scale back fall commitments
  and/or watch for a delayed or shifted window rather than assuming Oct–Nov exactly repeats.
- PTO must be committed 14+ days ahead per date — start locking in fall-window weekday PTO once
  live signals confirm, no later than mid-Sept-equivalent (doy ~260) so commitments land in time.
- Keep a small reserve (~1 day_1.5 or 2 overnight worth of budget/PTO) for the April early-spike
  window (doy ~90–119) IF live pier/fishdope data in April looks like a repeat of season 1's small
  early pulse (day_1_5 ypa 3.0 / overnight 1.78, but n was tiny — don't over-trust it blind).
- Boat selection: don't default to `ctx.pick_boat` (most-active, not best-producing) without
  checking recent trips/fishdope boat-level counts at each nightly call, when the briefing allows
  distinguishing scheduled boats' recent performance.
- `strategy.py` stays the no-op placeholder. Nightly manual decisions remain the primary control
  since we still only have ~1.3 seasons of noisy data; revisit encoding rules into standing code
  once season 2's fall window either confirms or contradicts season 1's pattern.

## To check next planning turn (or as soon as April data arrives)
- Does an April spike appear in season 2 doy ~90–120? Compare live pier SST / fishdope / early
  trip ypa against season 1's same window.
- How does ONI/PDO/MEI actually evolve through season 2's spring/summer — does La Niña relax
  (like season 1 did, in reverse) or deepen/persist through the whole year?
- Once fall-window doy data exists for season 2, re-run: yt/angler by class×doy-bucket, and the
  CUTI-14d / SST-7d trailing correlations pooled across both seasons — see if they hold, sharpen,
  or wash out.
- Check whether `sla` ever gets populated — would let the persona's actual sea-level-anomaly
  thesis be tested directly instead of via SST/CUTI proxies.
- Keep building the "boats that outperform" list at Seaforth/H&M/Point Loma for day_1_5/overnight
  if a boat-level pattern holds up in season 2 too.
